# Omerica Heat Rescue: scientific citations and parameter provenance

Reviewed 22 October 2026. This ledger distinguishes established mathematics from this project's synthetic assumptions. A cited scientific publication is a reference, not a bundled software dependency, a commercial license, or validation of this simulator. No paper PDFs, figures, abstracts, experimental datasets, pretrained weights, or Valency search-result exports are included in this release. Bibliographic records are available in [SOURCES.bib](SOURCES.bib).

## Equations and implemented methods

| Implemented element | Equation or method | Source and scope |
|---|---|---|
| Thermoelectric voltage and load power, `model.js::tegAt` | `Voc = alpha (Th − Tc)`; `I = Voc / (R + RL)`; `P = I² RL` | Ferrotec, [Thermoelectric Reference Guide §13.2](https://thermal.ferrotec.com/technology/thermoelectric-reference-guide/thermalref13/). Established constant-property generator equations; our implementation and explanatory text are written for this project. No Ferrotec module is simulated or endorsed. |
| Heat entering and leaving each tile | `Qh = alpha Th I − I²R/2 + K(Th − Tc)`; `Qc = alpha Tc I + I²R/2 + K(Th − Tc)` | Same [§13](https://thermal.ferrotec.com/technology/thermoelectric-reference-guide/thermalref13/). Absolute temperatures are in kelvin. These equations imply `Qh − Qc = P` for the chosen resistive load. |
| Module constants `alpha`, `R`, `K` (background only; the values used are round assumptions) | Reference-module temperature dependence | Ferrotec, [Thermoelectric Reference Guide §11](https://thermal.ferrotec.com/technology/thermoelectric-reference-guide/thermalref11/). Cited in `model.js`; no Ferrotec coefficient table is used. |
| Matched electrical load | `RL = R` | For fixed face temperatures, differentiating `P = Voc² RL / (R + RL)²` gives its maximum at `RL = R`. This is a maximum-power condition at fixed temperatures, not a maximum-efficiency guarantee for the coupled thermal system. Conversion electronics and their losses are omitted. |
| Plate and water temperature dynamics | `C dT/dt = sum(Qin) − sum(Qout)`; conductive paths `Q = G(T1 − T2)` | [MIT thermodynamics course notes, §6.7.2](https://web.mit.edu/snively/www/2_005%20Coursenotes-1.pdf). Conservation of energy applied separately to the hot plate, cold plate, and well-mixed water volume. Network topology and conductances are project assumptions. |
| Water heat transport | `Qflow = mdot cp (Twater − Tin)` | Bosch Industrial Heat, [Heat output](https://www.boiler-planning.com/en/hotwater/planning/fundamentals/heat-output). Its listed water heat capacity supports the representative constant `cp = 4183 J/(kg K)`; the app does not model its temperature or pressure dependence. |
| Backup electrical pumping cost | `Ppump = delta_p mdot / (rho eta)` | US Department of Energy, [Test for Pumping System Efficiency, Tip Sheet 4, September 2005](https://www1.eere.energy.gov/manufacturing/tech_assistance/pdfs/test_pumping_system__pumping_systemts4.pdf). The tip sheet supports the system-efficiency concept; the SI form `Ppump = delta_p mdot / (rho eta)` is the standard hydraulic-power relation and is not taken from the tip sheet. Our pressure-flow relation and efficiency are assumed, not fitted pump data. |
| Time integration | Classical explicit fourth-order Runge–Kutta, maximum step `0.25 s` | Matt Durey, MIT, [Nonlinear dynamical systems, 3 October 2019, numerical solution section](https://math.mit.edu/classes/18.353J/Lectures/Matt_s_Notes/2Dsystems.pdf). The numerical method is standard; JavaScript implementation is local. A small time step and energy-balance tests do not establish real-device accuracy. |
| Initial equilibrium | Newton iteration on three heat-balance residuals, finite-difference Jacobian, pivoted linear solve | Standard numerical root finding implemented locally. Initial conditions solve each candidate's all-open equilibrium; preparation energy is excluded. Solver tolerance and iteration limits are numerical choices, not measured properties. |
| Gaussian-process regression | Two independent GP predictors, one for net energy and one for peak temperature | Rasmussen and Williams, [Gaussian Processes for Machine Learning, Chapter 2, equations 2.25–2.26 and Algorithm 2.1](https://gaussianprocess.org/gpml/chapters/RW2.pdf). Cholesky factorization and triangular solves implement prediction without an external GP library. No book code, pages, or figures are distributed. |
| GP covariance | Squared-exponential/RBF kernel with separate length scales | Rasmussen and Williams, [Chapter 4, equation 4.9](https://gaussianprocess.org/gpml/chapters/RW4.pdf). Fixed length scales, output standardization, and diagonal regularization are disclosed project settings rather than learned physical truths. |
| Sequential experiment selection | Fit from completed trials, then choose an untested candidate using expected improvement | Snoek, Larochelle and Adams, [Practical Bayesian Optimization of Machine Learning Algorithms (2012)](https://arxiv.org/abs/1206.2944). Established methodology; the app does not claim a new optimizer. |
| Temperature-constrained selection | Expected improvement weighted by predicted probability of satisfying the temperature limit | Gelbart, Snoek and Adams, [Bayesian Optimization with Unknown Constraints (2014)](https://arxiv.org/abs/1403.5607). A lightweight local implementation inspired by the established approach, not a reproduction of that paper's experiments. Predicted feasibility is not a safety certificate. |
| Normal cumulative distribution | `Phi(z) = (1 + erf(z / sqrt(2))) / 2`; polynomial approximation to `erf` | Abramowitz and Stegun, *Handbook of Mathematical Functions* (1964), §7.1.26, p. 299: [original page scan](https://personal.math.ubc.ca/~cbm/aands/page_299.htm), [NIST bibliographic record](https://www.nist.gov/mathematics-statistics/handbook-mathematical-functions-abramowitz-and-stegun). Arithmetic implementation of the formula; the book scan is not bundled. |
| Seeded trial ordering | Mulberry32 generator ([Ettinger](https://gist.github.com/tommyettinger/46a874533244883189143505d203312c); [bryc JavaScript form](https://github.com/bryc/code/blob/master/jshash/PRNGs.md)), Fisher–Yates shuffle | Algorithm provenance and applicable code license are recorded in the release's third-party notices. Randomness controls reproducibility and proposal tie order; it is not cryptographic randomness. |

## Synthetic assumptions, not source measurements

The current release deliberately uses independent round thermoelectric parameters. Earlier development versions used a Ferrotec polynomial example; those coefficient tables have been removed. Results from that earlier model are not evidence for the current model. Refer to the current benchmark artifact and its model/protocol version.

| Parameter group | Current values | Provenance / limitation |
|---|---|---|
| Generator tile | `alpha = 0.05 V/K`, `R = 2.5 ohm`, `K = 0.6 W/K`; six tiles total | Independent synthetic benchmark choices, held constant. No commercial module datasheet, manufacturer coefficient table, or material measurement is used. |
| Manual heat loads | Three branches at `200 W` each | Hypothetical examples. |
| AI training heat loads | `240 / 200 / 160 W` | Hypothetical uneven workload, fixed before evaluation. |
| Nominal room/supply | `25°C` | Imposed boundaries. Maintaining the supply temperature requires real cooling energy that this model does not calculate. |
| Water properties | `cp = 4183 J/(kg K)`; `rho = 997 kg/m³` | Representative constant approximations. Heat capacity reference above; density is an assumed room-temperature approximation, not a measured test condition. |
| Thermal capacities | Hot `900`, cold `450`, water `418.3 J/K` | Chosen lumped capacities. Water capacity corresponds to an assumed `0.1 kg` with the stated heat capacity. |
| Thermal conductances | Bypass `4`; cold-to-water `25`; hot-to-room `1`; cold-to-room `2`; water-to-room `0.5 W/K` | Hypothetical network conductances, not measured geometry or calibrated contacts. |
| Main flow | `0.01 kg/s` per nominal branch | Assumed regulated independent branches; no pressure redistribution or shared hydraulic solution. |
| Electrical overhead | Fixed main cooling `3 W`; added recovery cost `0.9 W` | Assumed costs. The objective subtracts the incremental `0.9 W` and backup pumping, excluding the already-existing main cooling draw. |
| Manual backup | `0.005 kg/s`, fixed `0.5 W` when enabled for a fault | Teaching illustration only. This differs from the AI's temperature-only controller and flow-dependent cost. |
| AI backup pressure | `delta_p = 25000 Pa × (mdot / 0.005 kg/s)²` | Assumed circuit resistance, not a manufacturer pump curve or measured pressure drop. |
| AI pump efficiency | `25%` | Assumed overall electrical-to-hydraulic efficiency. |
| Design choices | Counts sum to 6; trigger `66 / 70 / 74 / 78°C`; backup fraction `0.25 / 0.5 / 0.75 / 1` | Project-defined 448-candidate search domain. These settings are not recommended hardware limits. |
| Controller | Temperature only, updated every second; `2°C` hysteresis | Project policy. It receives no fault-location or future-test signal. Backup may consume power on an otherwise healthy branch. |
| Temperature constraint | Peak modeled hot plate at or below `80°C` | Illustrative benchmark criterion, not a CPU-junction rating or certified safe temperature. |
| Train/test protocol | Three `600 s` training trials; six `900 s` held-out cases; fault starts at `30 s` | Project-created synthetic fault suite. Held-out conditions vary remaining flow, workload, room/supply temperature and conductance. See `TRAIN_SCENARIOS` and `HOLDOUT_SCENARIOS` in [experiment-model.js](experiment-model.js). |
| GP settings | Four starting observations; fixed RBF length scales; small diagonal regularization; finite trial budget | Computational choices listed in `PLANNER_PROTOCOL` in [ai-planner.js](ai-planner.js). Surrogate variance is not calibrated hardware uncertainty. |
| Reported results | Calculated energy, temperatures and feasibility | Generated by this simulator. No physical experiments, real server telemetry, external benchmark datasets or pretrained model weights. Saved verification runs are labeled separately from live runs. |

The net objective is the worst scenario's integral of generated tile power minus incremental recovery and backup electrical costs. All designs are selected on training outcomes before held-out evaluation. This is a project-defined objective and evaluation protocol. Chiller energy, electrical conversion losses, pump heating of coolant, internal CPU hot spots, turbulent flow and temperature-dependent material properties remain outside scope.

## Prior work and novelty boundaries

- Zhu et al., [Heat to Power: Thermal Energy Harvesting and Recycling for Warm Water-Cooled Datacenters](https://fangmingliu.github.io/files/H2P-camera-ready.pdf): hardware thermoelectric heat recovery, water/cooling settings and workloads. Basic heat recovery is established.
- Bao, Zhou and Li, [Physics-based machine learning optimization of thermoelectric assembly for maximizing waste heat recovery](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.energy.2024.132821), *Energy* 307 (2024), 132821: data-center TEG optimization and net power accounting already exist. Publisher abstract/excerpts only were inspected.
- Otaki, Nonaka and Yamada, [Machine learning thermal circuit network model for thermal design optimization of electronic circuit board layout with transient heating chips](https://arxiv.org/abs/2008.13571), preprint 2020; journal version 2022: transient thermal networks plus Bayesian optimization already exist.
- Liu, [Generative Design for Direct-to-Chip Liquid Cooling for Data Centers](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.10941), 2026: iterative cooling-channel design with thermal feedback.
- [Optimal Reconfiguration of Thermoelectric Generation System Under Heterogeneous Temperature Difference](https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/energy-research/articles/10.3389/fenrg.2022.967167/full), 2022: thermoelectric array reconfiguration is established prior work.
- [Bi-objective Bayesian Optimization for Multi-variable Performance Enhancement of Non-uniform Thermoelectric Generators](https://papers.ssrn.com/sol3/papers.cfm?abstract_id=5645576), SSRN preprint, 2025: Bayesian optimization for TEGs. Abstract-only scope; no claim about unseen full text.
- [Prediction-Based Fast Thermoelectric Generator Reconfiguration for Energy Harvesting from Vehicle Radiators](https://arxiv.org/abs/1804.01574), 2018; and Wang et al., [Global sensitivity analysis and optimization of multi-stage TEG based on random and fuzzy mixed input variables](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.applthermaleng.2024.123212), 2024: prediction, reconfiguration and uncertainty are not new individually.

Our candidate contribution is a reproducible, budgeted joint placement-and-backup fault benchmark. No first-ever invention, patent clearance, physical efficiency gain or statistical superiority beyond the reported simulations is established by this literature check. See [research-gap.md](research-gap.md) for comparison scope.

## Valency and rights boundary

Valency was used for nine research searches, followed by independent primary-source checks. It is not shipped, called by the app, or used to validate physics. Its [official terms, effective 29 September 2026](https://www.valency.io/terms/), limit free-tier use to research/evaluation/non-commercial experimentation and require a separate commercial license for productization or exposing its functionality, content or outputs to others. No public hackathon waiver was verified. [Sponsor listing](https://llmhackathon.github.io/sponsors/) confirms sponsorship, not resale permission. Raw search exports and abstracts are excluded from this release.

External publications keep their own rights. Citation does not make them open source, and the project's license does not relicense them. The U.S. Copyright Office distinguishes methods and facts from their protected expression ([Circular 33](https://www.copyright.gov/circs/circ33.pdf)). This project implements and cites mathematical methods without distributing source publications. That distinction is not a patent, trademark, contract, or worldwide commercial-clearance opinion.


## 3D assembly view

The additional assembly scene uses [Three.js 0.170.0](https://registry.npmjs.org/three/-/three-0.170.0.tgz) as a local MIT-licensed renderer; see [license and provenance](vendor/three/provenance.json) and [full MIT notice](vendor/three/LICENSE). Server geometry, plumbing, labels and camera controls are original procedural presentation code. No reference-project mesh, texture or source code was reused.

Visual mood references (a hobbyist router build and a data-center assembly illustration) informed materials, lighting and camera framing only; no geometry, images or code from them were used.

The manual scene still uses three assumed 200 W branches. The AI benchmark still uses its separately documented unequal loads. Exploded spacing, particles, decorative fan motion and color mapping are illustrations, not measured dimensions, CFD, calibrated velocity, or additional simulated energy accounting. Current temperatures/power are supplied by the unchanged solver; the AI proposal viewer displays a proposed layout without invented outcomes. Source hashes are checked in `../SCIENCE-INTEGRITY.json`.
